newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit stays in tight range, ends up vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit stays in tight range, ends up vs dollar.

text.p: The ringgit closed slightly higher against the dollar after rates were trapped in a tight trading range throughout Monday's session due to lack of fresh factors, dealers said.
They said short covering supported the ringgit but gains were limited by commercial demand for the dollar.
"There was some demand for both currencies but movements were tight throughout as there were no fresh leads," said a dealer with a local bank. He expects the trend to continue through the week.
Talk of better trade figures for August, expected to be released this week, also helped the ringgit, dealers said.
Malaysia recorded a trade deficit of 624.5 million ringgit in July.
Dealers said any ringgit rise is likely to be capped by commercial dollar demand.
They said the market is waiting to take its direction from the 1997 budget, to be unveiled on October 25.
At the local 1000 GMT close, the ringgit was at 2.5042/52 per dollar against 2.5060/70 on Friday.
